title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 'Analysis situs (4e mouture)' notes (1986) build a combinatorial model of the tame topology of the line (and polygonal figures). M is the set of 'elementary cells' attached to an ordered set of abscissae: points P_x and open segments S_{ab} with a<b. Cells of all subdivisions are allowed, since S_{a'b'} lies in S_{ab} for a≤a'<b'≤b. |Z| is the geometric realization. A figure or préfigure is a finite set of cells. For such a set Φ, supp°(Φ) (the 'open support', 'rapport') is the set of all cells of M, at any level of subdivision, whose relative interior lies in the realization of Φ. Omb (shadow) and Omb° are the closed and open shadow relations. The previous page reduces the computation of supp° of an arbitrary polygonal set to connected pieces (additivity over connected components) and then to three steps. This page does steps (a) and the start of (b).

(a) Irreducible cases.
(i) For X a cell, write X̃ for its closure (X with its boundary points). The support of X is defined as supp°(X̃). Grothendieck states it equals Omb(X) (a theorem, referred back to p. 91), which is trivially {Z : |Z| ⊂ |X|}. Explicitly: supp{P_a} = {P_a}; supp S̃_ab = {P_x, a≤x≤b} ∪ {S_{a'b'}, a≤a'<b'≤b}.
(ii) For α ⊂ ∂X = {P_a, P_b}, the half-open or open segment X̃∖α has supp°(X̃∖α) = supp X ∖ α.

A more elegant reformulation:
(α) For every cell X, supp° X = Omb° X = {Z : Z ≤° X}, i.e. cells whose relative interior is inside the interior of X. So supp° S_ab = {P_x, a<x<b} ∪ {S_{a'b'}, a≤a'<b'≤b}.
(β) For β ⊂ ∂S_ab, supp°(S_ab ∪ β) = Omb°(S_ab) ∪ β. A margin note records that α and β are complementary in ∂X.

(b) General case begins. Take T a chain ('développement' Dév*(L)) with card T ≥ 3, origin a and end b, α ⊂ ∂T = {a,b} with complement β, and Ω = F_T ∖ α (the polygonal figure on T minus α). The next page states that supp Ω = Omb(S̃_ab)∖α = Omb°(S_ab) ∪ β. It is proved via a gluing lemma: supp°(Φ ∪ Ψ) = supp°Φ ∪ supp°Ψ when some cell X is positionally between Φ and Ψ.

Purpose: an explicit, subdivision-invariant description of the 'support' of polygonal sets. Through it, figures that differ only by subdivision are identified, giving a combinatorial foundation of 1-dimensional tame topology.
errors: No mathematical errors. The formulas are internally consistent: the closed segment contains both endpoints, the open segment neither, and the half-open cases are obtained by removing α or adding β. Sub-segments S_{a'b'} with a'=a or b'=b are correctly kept in the open support, since their relative interiors lie inside the open segment.
Minor notational drift: (ii) is first written with 'α ⊂ {P_a,P_b}' and then corrected to specify X = S_ab. The heading uses α ∈ {P_a,P_b} while the text uses α ⊂ {P_a,P_b}.

ideas.what: Open support / open shadow of a cell in the poset of cells of all subdivisions of the line: supp°X = {Z : interior of Z ⊂ interior of X}; closed version Omb(X) = {Z : |Z| ⊂ |X|}
ideas.modern_name: Subdivision-invariant (stable) description of locally closed polyhedral sets; cells of a refinement lying in a stratum; closure/star relations in the face poset of the colimit over subdivisions
ideas.usually_credited_to: PL topology (subdivision theory, Whitehead, Zeeman); tame topology / o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is advocated programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but this combinatorial 'analysis situs' formalism is unpublished as far as I know.

ideas.what: Computation of supports of half-open segments by removing (α) or adding (β) complementary boundary points
ideas.modern_name: Locally closed cells; constructible subsets of a 1-dimensional cell complex

ideas.what: Reduction of the support computation for a polygonal chain to elementary cells via additivity and a gluing lemma
ideas.modern_name: Mayer–Vietoris-type locality of supports under subdivision

missed.claim: This page belongs to Grothendieck's unpublished attempt (1986) at a purely combinatorial foundation of tame (polyhedral) topology. Points and segments of all subdivisions are treated as one poset M, with 'shadow' relations Omb/Omb° and supports supp/supp°. That framework itself is not in the literature. The page's own content, however, is elementary and routine.
missed.quote: Une autre façon (plus élégante) d'expliciter 2° est ainsi, ∀ X ∈ M, supp° X = Omb° X = { Z ∈ M | Z ≤° X }
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest as concrete evidence of how Grothendieck tried to realize the 'topologie modérée' programme of the Esquisse. It is loosely comparable to later combinatorial and o-minimal approaches, such as exit-path or stratified-space combinatorics. No new mathematical result appears on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are elementary verifications of how open and closed supports of points and (half-)open segments look across all subdivisions. The only notable aspect is that they belong to an unpublished combinatorial tame-topology programme.
transcription_corrections: Bottom of page: 'et T ≥ 3' should read 'card T ≥ 3' (the image shows 'card T ≥ 3').
Margin at top left reads roughly 'voyez aussi p. 91' (reference back to p. 91), consistent with 'Le résultat ici est connu (p. 91)'.
In (ii), the insertion above the line is 'X = S_ab' and precedes 'α ⊂ {P_a,P_b}'; the struck word is a false start, not 'et'.
